description: Estimate a Databricks workload's monthly cost from the figures the Field Guide states (list prices per DBU by compute type, DBUs an hour by SQL warehouse size and classic instance type, model serving prices for pay-per-token, provisioned throughput, GPU and CPU serving, Apps and Genie rates, the Lakebase floor, storage), as a range with its assumptions, and the price per unit under unit_prices. Every number carries its source sentence, section URL, date and the pricing page the guide cites. Where the guide has no figure (cloud VM prices, a serverless job's DBUs an hour, a model or instance type it does not list) it says so under gaps instead of guessing.

always_on.description: lakebase: an always-on 0.5 CU floor (the one Lakebase figure the guide quotes)

compute.description: jobs and all_purpose: serverless or classic; sql_warehouse: serverless, pro, classic, or lakehouse_rt (Beta) priced from DBUs you give

days_per_month.description: Days it runs a month (default 30 with hours_per_day)

dbus_per_hour.description: DBUs the compute uses an hour, when the guide has no figure for its shape (a serverless job, an instance type it does not list): from system.billing.usage or Databricks' pricing calculator

dbus_per_month.description: Or the DBUs a month outright

dbus_per_user.description: genie: each user's Genie DBUs a month

input_tokens_millions.description: model_serving, pay_per_token: input tokens a month, in millions

instance_type.description: jobs or all_purpose, classic: the AWS instance type (m5.xlarge, m5.2xlarge, m6i.xlarge, m7i.xlarge, r5.xlarge, c5.2xlarge, i3.xlarge, i3.2xlarge are in the guide)

instances.description: jobs or all_purpose, classic: instances in the cluster, the driver counted as one; model_serving cpu: Medium configurations

max_clusters.description: sql_warehouse: the most clusters it scales out to; the estimate ranges from clusters to max_clusters

model.description: model_serving, pay_per_token or provisioned_throughput: the model, as in 'Llama 3.3 70B' or 'claude-sonnet-5.5'

model_units.description: model_serving, provisioned_throughput: model units (default 50, the block the rates are quoted for; a reservation takes multiples of 50 and bills every hour of its term)

output_tokens_millions.description: model_serving, pay_per_token: output tokens a month, in millions

serving.description: model_serving: pay_per_token, provisioned_throughput, gpu or cpu (omit for every price the guide states)

size.description: apps: medium (the default), large or xlarge; sql_warehouse: the t-shirt size, 2x-small, x-small, small, medium, large, x-large, 2x-large, 3x-large, 4x-large, 5x-large (DBUs an hour per cluster, from the guide); model_serving with serving gpu: t4, a10g, a10g-4, a10g-8, l40s, rtx-pro-6000, a100-40gb-8, a100-80gb-8, h100, h100-8

workload.description: jobs, all_purpose (interactive notebooks), sql_warehouse, apps, genie, lakebase, model_serving or storage

name: estimate_cost

build.description: The commit of the deploy that answered

calculator.description: For an interactive view: the inputs as asked and this workload's rates from the guide, to recompute the estimate locally. Not in the text result.

as_of.description: The date the guide gives for the figure, YYYY-MM-DD

dated.description: How the figure is dated: the guide's own date, or its chapter's last update

items.description: A pricing or documentation page the guide cites for it
What the guide has no figure for, so the estimate leaves it out

index_built.description: When this deploy's index was built (ISO 8601)

monthly_usd.description: The estimate, a month; null where the guide has no figure for it (see gaps)

ttlMs.description: How long this answer may be kept before asking again, in milliseconds

unit_prices.description: The price per unit the guide's figures give (a cluster-hour, a million tokens, an endpoint-hour), with or without usage

per.description: The unit, as in '1M output tokens' or 'a medium cluster-hour'

title: Estimate Databricks cost
